__comment: The operator dashboard §41 asks to be checked in: the §14 metric list, plus error rate by type.
Grafana schema, because Prometheus and Grafana are what Micrometer and the actuator already
assume — a dashboard in a format nobody deploys is a document rather than a dashboard.
Every query below is over metrics this repository actually emits. There is a test that asserts
that: a panel querying a metric nobody registers is a panel that reads 'No data' during the one
incident it was kept for, and nothing about it looks wrong until then.
title: Kitbash

panels.title: Generations per minute, by outcome
panels.description: §14: generation duration and outcome. 'cached' is a hit served without rendering — it is a success that cost nothing, and folding it into 'succeeded' hides the cache working.

panels.title: Generation duration
panels.description: §2 budgets generation in tens of milliseconds. The 99th percentile is the one that matters: a mean stays flat while the slowest selection doubles.

panels.title: Cache hit rate
panels.description: §27: the number that says whether determinism is holding in production. A rate that collapses means the output stopped being reproducible, which is worth noticing before a user reports two different zips for one selection.

panels.title: Rejections by type
panels.description: §14 and §39. The breakdown rather than the rate: a code that suddenly dominates is usually a catalog problem wearing a user's clothes — a spike in CAPABILITY_UNSATISFIED means a recipe declared a requires nothing provides.

panels.title: Recipe usage
panels.description: §14. From the resolved lock rather than the selection, so a recipe the resolver added counts as used — counting selections would say a database is unpopular because nobody picks one on purpose.

panels.title: Matrix pass rate
panels.description: §14. Derived by the API from the results the nightly publishes (kitbash-38), because the matrix is a batch job with nothing scraping it. Which cell is red is on the status page; this is the trend.

panels.title: Verification queue and runs
panels.description: §12, §37. Depth says whether four workers is the right number; outcomes say whether the runs are working. A queue that is never deep and a run that always fails look identical on depth alone.
